title: Relationship quality in older age – influences of dyadic coping, self-construction, stress, depression, caregiving burden, and resilience
summary:
The BALANCE study examines how older people experience their relationships and which factors contribute to a good quality of relationship. With increasing age, issues such as health, stress, or caregiving responsibilities can have a significant impact on relationships. The aim of the study is to better understand which conditions promote or hinder cohabitation and well-being in long-term relationships.

The study is aimed at people aged 65 and over who are in a relationship. Participation is online via an anonymous questionnaire. It is possible to participate alone or together with your partner. If both partners participate, their answers are matched using an anonymous code in order to better understand couple dynamics.

The survey contains questions on topics such as relationship quality, joint stress management (dyadic coping), self-image and independence in the relationship, mental well-being, depression and, if applicable, care burden and resilience. The results will contribute to a better understanding of how older couples in different life situations maintain their well-being and their relationship.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Sufficient knowledge of German to understand information about the study and actively participate in the online survey
- Living in a romantic relationship
- Access to a computer, tablet, or smartphone with an internet connection
Exclusion criteria:
- Singles or individuals without a current partner
- Individuals who attempt to participate in the study multiple times (e.g., by registering twice or entering the code twice)
